TrendPlain Glass Olive Oil Sprayer vs Evo Original: Best Refillable Oil Sprayer (2026)

$7.99 TrendPlain 16oz Glass Sprayer vs $19.99 Evo Original — one's a glass bottle with dual pour-and-spray, the other's a designer plastic mister with a fan nozzle. Which refillable sprayer earns its spot on your counter?

Published August 15, 2026 · Based on verified Amazon product data and real customer outcomes

If you cook with any regularity, you know the frustration. You buy a can of non-stick spray, use it for two weeks, and then it runs out — or worse, the nozzle clogs. You're left with a half-full can and a stubborn streak of resentment toward the entire concept of aerosolized cooking oil.

Refillable oil sprayers solve this. You buy a quality bottle once, fill it with whatever oil you prefer (olive, avocado, sesame, even vinegar), and you're set indefinitely. No more cans, no more propellants, no more wondering what's actually in that spray.

The TrendPlain 16oz Glass Olive Oil Sprayer and the Evo Original Oil Sprayer are two of the most popular refillable options on Amazon. But they take very different approaches. One is a glass bottle with dual pour-and-spray functionality for $7.99. The other is a designer plastic mister with a fan-pattern nozzle for $19.99. Here's how they stack up for real-world cooking.

Quick Verdict

Buy the TrendPlain Glass Sprayer if: You want a glass bottle (no plastic leaching concerns), the flexibility of both spray and pour modes, precise portion control (0.15g per spray), and lifetime customer support — all for less than eight bucks. It's the smarter buy for everyday cooking.

Buy the Evo Original if: You want the largest capacity available (24oz), a proven fan-pattern nozzle that covers more surface area per spray, and a design from the Michael Graves Design Group. It's the premium, established name in oil sprayers.

Our pick: The TrendPlain Glass Sprayer. It costs 60% less than the Evo, stores your oil in glass (which is inert and doesn't degrade in heat or sunlight like plastic can), gives you both spray and pour capability in one bottle, and backs everything with a lifetime support guarantee. The Evo is a fine product, but the TrendPlain simply offers more value for most home cooks.

🎨 Evo Original Oil Sprayer (24oz)

$19.99 on Amazon

The Evo Original is the established name in refillable oil sprayers. Designed by the Michael Graves Design Group, it's been a kitchen staple for years and has a loyal following among serious home cooks.

Evo's unique fan-pattern nozzle is its standout feature. Instead of a conical mist, it sprays oil in a wide fan shape — similar to a pump sprayer. This covers more surface area per squeeze, which is genuinely useful for coating large pans, griddle surfaces, or baking sheets quickly. Each spray delivers 1.35ml — about 9x more oil per pump than the TrendPlain.

The 24oz capacity is the largest we've seen in a refillable sprayer. If you cook in volume or go through oil quickly, you'll refill less often. The bottle is made from BPA-free, latex-free, DEHP-free plastic — it's shatter-resistant, which is a real advantage if you have a tile floor or clumsy hands.

Thoughtful touches include a twist-on funnel for mess-free refilling and three reusable bands to label different oils (olive, avocado, canola, etc.). The green color is distinctive and looks fine on a counter, though the plastic body feels less premium than glass.

Key specs: 24oz capacity, BPA-free plastic, fan-pattern spray nozzle, 1.35ml per spray, includes twist-on funnel + 3 labeling bands, hand wash recommended, designed by Michael Graves Design Group.

Why TrendPlain Wins for Most Kitchens

The price difference is hard to ignore. At $7.99, the TrendPlain costs 60% less than the Evo at $19.99. That's not pocket change — it's the difference between buying one sprayer and buying two, or buying a sprayer and a bottle of quality olive oil to fill it with.

Glass vs. plastic is a meaningful distinction. Glass is chemically inert — it doesn't react with oil, doesn't leach anything, and doesn't degrade over time. Olive oil is sensitive to heat, light, and oxygen; storing it in glass (especially tinted glass) preserves its flavor longer than plastic. The Evo's plastic body is BPA-free and food-safe, but for long-term oil storage, glass is objectively better.

Dual spray-and-pour is genuinely useful. When you're air-frying, you want a fine mist that coats evenly. When you're drizzling over a salad or filling a pan, you want a steady stream. The TrendPlain does both with one bottle. The Evo only sprays — if you need a pour, you need a separate dispenser.

Precise portion control matters. Each TrendPlain spray delivers exactly 0.15g of oil. If you're tracking calories or macros, that level of precision is valuable. The Evo sprays 1.35ml per pump — nearly 9x as much. For light coating, that's overkill.

"I've owned a Misto, I've owned an Evo, and I've owned a cheap no-name sprayer. This TrendPlain is the first one that actually delivers a consistent fine mist without clogging — and it pours too." — Verified Amazon buyer

When the Evo Original Is the Better Choice

Larger capacity matters if you cook in volume. The Evo holds 24oz to TrendPlain's 16oz. For a big family or someone who cooks multiple meals a day, that's fewer refills. The plastic body is also shatter-resistant — drop it on a tile floor and it bounces instead of breaks.

The fan-pattern spray is genuinely different. If you're regularly coating large surfaces — a griddle for pancakes, a massive baking sheet for roasted vegetables, a paella pan — the Evo's wide fan pattern covers more ground faster. It's a practical advantage for high-volume cooking.

Established brand with a track record. Evo has been making oil sprayers for years. The Michael Graves design is recognizable, the build quality is consistent, and you can find replacement parts if needed. It's the safe, known-quantity choice.

The Bottom Line

Our Take

The TrendPlain Glass Olive Oil Sprayer is the smarter buy for virtually every home cook. It's made of glass — which is the right material for storing cooking oils — gives you both spray and pour capabilities, delivers a precise 0.15g mist for portion control, and costs just $7.99. That's less than half the price of the Evo, and it comes with a lifetime support guarantee. Amazon customers agree: it's earned Amazon's Choice and over 20,000 people buy it every month.

The Evo Original is a capable product with a loyal following, a larger 24oz capacity, and an innovative fan-pattern nozzle. If you cook in high volume, prefer plastic for durability, or just want the established name-brand option, it will serve you well. But for the price of one Evo, you could buy two TrendPlains — one for olive oil and one for avocado oil — and still have money left over.
